newsitem.title: CHINA: HK gold ends up on shortcovering, overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends up on shortcovering, overseas buying.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended up on Thursday compared to New York's previous close, helped by shortcovering and European buying, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$319.30/80 on Thursday compared to New York's previous close at US$318.00/50 on Wednesday.
After a quiet morning session, European buying in early afternoon helped edge gold prices up to intra-day highs of $319.60/320/10 per ounce, before dipping back slightly at the close.
"People are shortcovering ahead of the weekend," said one trader.
Trade direction remained uncertain, traders said.
Physical demand had continued, although price fluctuations meant buyers were still wary, sources said.
Local tael gold ended HK$32 up at HK$2,960.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -6.00 from its previous fix at +1.00.
